stories.headline: Trump to announce Audi SUV plant in Georgia amid tariff push
stories.bodyText: US President Donald Trump is expected to announce on Saturday that Volkswagen's premium subsidiary Audi plans to build an assembly plant in Georgia that will produce 200,000 SUVs annually, a government official told Reuters. Trump, who has pressured automakers to move production to the United States and has hiked tariffs on autos, steel, aluminum and parts, plans to make the announcement in Georgia near where Audi intends to build the plant, which is expected to assemble the Q7, Q8 and Q9 SUVs. Audi is also expected to announce plans to build 25,000 vehicles in South Carolina, the official added. Some of the vehicles, which are currently built in Europe, would be exported, the source added. Audi declined to comment. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The vehicles to be produced in South Carolina will be assembled at VW's off-road brand Scout Motors' $2 billion plant that is under construction in Blythewood, South Carolina. COMPETITIVE RACES IN GEORGIA Georgia has competitive midterm election races for US Senate and governor and Trump is eager to make the case that his auto tariffs are helping the US economy. Critics say the tariffs have led to higher vehicle prices. .Independent practice licence in Georgia, not junior doctor role, allows candidates to take FMGE: NMC. Trump's decision to cut incentives for electric vehicles has led to a significant reduction in US EV and battery production. Overall US vehicle and parts employment has fallen since Trump took office. A gold Audi with manufacturer license plates was parked outside Trump's rally in Perry, Georgia. Audi sales have fallen for two consecutive years and slid 7% in the first half of 2026 as fierce competition in China and US tariffs hit demand. Audi's US sales are down 16% this year. Audi's Neckarsulm plant in southwest Germany is one of four German Volkswagen plants facing possible closure after 2030. In July, Toyota said it would spend $3.6 billion to build a 2.5-million-square-foot (232,000-square-metre) truck assembly line on its San Antonio, Texas, manufacturing campus and shift some truck production to the US from Mexico. The Japanese automaker said the expansion would be completed by 2030, creating 2,000 jobs. Honda Motor is considering building a US assembly plant, but has warned it may not unless the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement on trade is extended. Hyundai said last year if it had certainty about USMCA it "would immediately unlock over $20 billion in new American investments."

stories.headline: Shops looted, streets ablaze as 'anti-system' riots rock Barcelona
stories.bodyText: A total of 100 people were arrested in Barcelona on Saturday evening after hooded demonstrators who participated in an anti-establishment rally looted shops and set fire to street furniture around the city's central Plaza de Catalunyaan. Núria Parlon, the interior minister for the Spanish region of Catalonia, said around 25% of those arrested were minors. More than 30 fires were set and 14 stores vandalised or looted in a part of town popular with tourists and weekend shoppers, she added. Demonstrators were called in social media posts to a movement "against the system." .70,000 police on streets as France mounts huge security operation ahead of protesters march. The posts also used the slogan "Institut Indignats", a translation of the movement "Lyceés Indignés" which was used to rally students who have protested in France in recent weeks. In English, the phrases translate as "Indignant High School Student." Social media videos show people trapped inside shops including department store El Corte Ingles after shutters were lowered to prevent looting. Other posts showed hooded demonstrators dressed in black kicking in shop windows and making off with goods, in some cases encouraged by online viewers. Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni said acts of vandalism in the city "will not go unpunished", including legal consequences for the guardians of any minors involved.

stories.headline: Team India's massive T20I record goes unnoticed; team miles ahead of Pakistan
stories.deck: India became the first team to play 300 men's T20 Internationals and also recorded their 200th win in the format. They reached the milestone in style, chasing down New Zealand's 180/5 with one ball to spare after losing five wickets for just 70 runs.
stories.bodyText:
India created a major T20 International record during their thrilling four-wicket win over New Zealand in Christchurch on Saturday. While the team celebrated a memorable victory, another achievement went largely unnoticed.
India became the first team to play 300 men's T20 Internationals and also recorded their 200th win in the format. They reached the milestone in style, chasing down New Zealand's 180/5 with one ball to spare after losing five wickets for just 70 runs.
The victory was made possible by an unbeaten 51 off 26 balls from Tilak Varma and an unbeaten 26 off 13 balls from Nitish Kumar Reddy. Their 69-run partnership for the seventh wicket took India to 181/6 in 19.5 overs.
India lead the world with 200 T20I wins
India have played 300 T20Is between 2006 and 2026, winning 200 matches, losing 83, tying seven and finishing 10 without a result. Their win-loss ratio stands at 2.409, which means they have won more than twice as many matches as they have lost.
Pakistan have played the most T20Is overall, with 304 matches, but have recorded 176 wins. India are ahead of them in the number of victories despite playing four fewer matches.
New Zealand, India's opponents in Christchurch, have played 269 T20Is and won 135. South Africa and England complete the top five teams on the list of total wins.
How India compare with other teams
India's 200 wins put them well ahead of the other major teams. Here is how the leading teams have performed in men's T20Is.
Figures cover the period up to 2026, as provided.
- Pakistan: They have played 304 matches, the most among these teams, and won 176. They have lost 116, tied four and had eight matches end without a result.
- New Zealand: They have won 135 of their 269 matches and lost 112. Ten matches were tied, while 12 had no result.
- South Africa: They have won 129 and lost 101 in 235 matches. Two matches were tied and three had no result.
- England: They have recorded 128 wins and 92 defeats in 233 matches. Two games were tied and 11 had no result.
- Australia: They have won 127 and lost 92 in 229 matches. Three games were tied and seven had no result.
- West Indies: They have played 260 matches, winning 111 and losing 133. Three games were tied and 13 had no result.
- Sri Lanka: They have won 105 and lost 130 in 243 matches. Six games were tied and two had no result.
- Uganda: They have won 101 of their 131 matches, with 27 defeats and three matches without a result. They have not tied a match.
- Afghanistan: They have recorded 99 wins and 65 defeats in 168 matches. Three games were tied and one had no result.
- Uganda's record is also notable. They have won 101 matches despite playing fewer than half as many games as India. However, India remain comfortably ahead in the total number of victories.
Tilak Varma leads India's stunning comeback
India's 200th T20I win did not come easily. Chasing 181, they were struggling at 70/5 in 10.5 overs after New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner took control with the ball.
Sanju Samson fell for 14, while Vaibhav Sooryavanshi managed only four. Abhishek Sharma scored 27 off 21 balls before Santner dismissed him. The left-arm spinner then removed captain Shreyas Iyer for seven and Axar Patel for 11, leaving India in serious trouble.
Naman Dhir gave India some hope with an aggressive 31 off 17 balls, including a four and three sixes. But his dismissal in the 15th over left the visitors needing another strong partnership.
Tilak took responsibility and played a calm yet attacking innings. He struck six fours and a six, reaching his half-century in 25 balls.
Nitish Reddy joins Tilak to seal the win
Nitish Kumar Reddy provided the perfect support, scoring an unbeaten 26 off 13 balls. The pair added 69 runs without being separated in just 30 balls.
Their partnership changed the match and took India to 181/6 in 19.5 overs. India won by four wickets, with one ball remaining.
Santner was New Zealand's best bowler, taking four wickets for 21 runs in four overs. However, his effort was not enough to stop India's record-breaking victory.
Phillips and Jacobs rescue New Zealand
Earlier, New Zealand recovered from a poor start to post 180/5 in their 20 overs. India's bowlers made early inroads. Arshdeep Singh dismissed Tim Seifert for seven, Prince Yadav removed Finn Allen for 16, and Bhuvneshwar Kumar sent back Daryl Mitchell for six.
New Zealand were reduced to 41/3, but Glenn Phillips and Bevon Jacobs rebuilt the innings with a 116-run partnership for the fourth wicket.
Phillips scored 70 off 43 balls, hitting four fours and four sixes. He brought up his half-century in 33 balls before Arshdeep dismissed him in the 18th over.
Jacobs made 58 off 46 balls, including five fours and a six, before Nitish Reddy removed him. Michael Bracewell then added a late burst with a four and a six as New Zealand finished at 180/5.
Arshdeep was India's leading bowler with figures of 2/33. Prince took one wicket for 30 runs, while Bhuvneshwar finished with 1/50. Axar conceded 28 runs in four overs without taking a wicket, and Reddy claimed 1/31 in three overs.
India's bowlers had kept New Zealand to a manageable total, but the hosts' strong middle-order partnership ensured the visitors had a challenging target. Tilak and Reddy eventually completed the chase, giving India a landmark win.

stories.headline: Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats
stories.deck: Ohio and Michigan, the 65-year-old former President blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices
stories.bodyText:
Former U.S. President Barack Obama delivered scathing criticisms of his successor, Donald Trump, at rallies on Saturday (October 24, 2026) in Ohio and Michigan to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
Democrats are attempting to wrest back control of one or both chambers of the U.S. Congress, which are currently controlled by Mr. Trump’s Republican party.
The former President retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his Democratic Party’s candidates.
In both states, the 65-year-old former President blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices.
“The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” Mr. Obama said in Ohio, where he rallied in support of former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown.
“Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for.”
“After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough,’” Mr. Obama declared in Cleveland. “We are voting for change right here in Ohio.”
Later, in Michigan, Mr. Obama campaigned for Abdul El-Sayed, from the party’s left wing, who is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers for the US Senate.
“Imagine the power duo of Abdul and Elissa,” Mr. Obama said, referring to the incumbent Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin, who is not up for election this year.
“You got a Muslim man, you got a Jewish woman fighting for you in the United States Senate. That’s something, Michigan, you can be proud of.”
Mr. Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in both states.
“Don’t procrastinate, don’t equivocate,” Mr. Obama said.
In Ohio, Mr. Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024.
Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both those races, but the results are expected to be close.
Mr. Obama also took digs at Mr. Trump’s renovation projects across the U.S. capital, including his botched renovation of the National Mall’s Reflecting Pool, his construction of a massive White House Ballroom and the gilded decorations he has adorned the Oval Office with during his second tenure.
“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Mr. Obama said, referring to the popular but indulgent American restaurant chain.
Nationally, polls also suggest that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives but face a much more competitive contest for the Senate.

briefs.headline: 'Fake passport to evade law': US asylum gamble blew gangster Bhau’s cover
briefs.deck: Himanshu Bhau and Neeraj Faridpuria attempted to exploit immigration laws to gain asylum in the US. Their plan backfired when they were detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Both individuals used fake passports to evade law enforcement for several years. Indian and US authorities confirmed Bhau's identity through cross-verification of their backgrounds. Efforts are underway to…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: A gamble to secure asylum in North America may have blown the cover of gangster Himanshu Bhau, one of north India’s notorious fugitives.
A day after TOI reported his detention in Nevada, sources said a brief, staged detention in Feb by Bhau and his aide Neeraj Faridpuria, designed to exploit legal loopholes and claim asylum, backfired and unravelled the plan.
The two face more than 25 criminal cases each across Delhi, Haryana and Punjab, including murder. Once the duo deliberately surrendered to immigration authorities to initiate asylum petitions, their biometrics and details were fed into US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) tracking system, which set off red flags.
Favourite route
Sources said fugitives from India were aggressively seeking this modus operandi. Lawrence Bishnoi’s brother, Anmol, too had tried it but was busted.
Currently lodged at the Henderson Detention Center under the jurisdiction of ICE, Bhau, sources said, used a forged passport under the alias Himanshu Singroha and evaded global law enforcement for over four years.
Most-wanted gangster
However, his calculated scheme to get himself deliberately detained along with his chief associate, Neeraj Faridpuria, who also was using a fake passport under the name Neeraj Kaushik, triggered their detention.
Once the duo deliberat-ely surrendered to immigration authorities to initiate asylum petitions, their biometrics and personal details were fed into the ICE track-ing system. Picking up critical leads from this database entry, Indian law enforcement agencies and US security counterparts dug deeper into the background of “Himanshu Singroha”.
Through cross-verification with local intelligen-ce sources, police contacts, and diplomatic counterparts, authorities confirmed that the individual in custody was indeed the high-profile fugitive Himanshu Bhau, a source said.
The details on the ICE portal, accessed by TOI, corroborate the details, including the fake name on the passport. Investigations further revealed Faridpuria also shifted his base from Portugal to the US in late 2025 before reuniting with Bhau.
The cops shared a dossier, including a photograph showing Faridpuria with guns and their other biometric details, which confirmed they were using forged documents. They were formally detained and information was shared with Indian agencies.
The two are linked to the 2024 murder in South Delhi’s Aya Nagar in which over 70 bullets were fired, another recent connected killing, the 2019 murder of Congress leader Vikas Chaudhary in Faridabad, and a shooting outside YouTuber Elvish Yadav’s residence.
Following confirmation of their detention in a Nevada prison, Indian agencies are working with US authorities to expedite their deportation. A special team is likely to be dispatched to expedite deportation.

briefs.headline: Andhra Pradesh braces for very severe cyclonic storm; landfall likely between Bapatla and Vizag on October 28
briefs.deck: Wind speed may go up to 130 kmph, say weather experts; IMD issues red alert for 13 districts on Otober 27 and 28
briefs.bodyText:
The cyclonic storm brewing over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said. It is likely to be the second highest in terms of intensity. Last year’s Montha was classified as a ‘severe cyclonic storm’.
The maximum sustained wind speed associated with a very severe cyclonic storm is likely to be between 118 km per hour and 221 km per hour. During Montha, the wind speed recorded at Machilipatnam was 65 kmph, while the wind speed this time may go up to 130 kmph, weather experts said.
According to the IMD bulletin released at 9.30 p.m. on Saturday, the well-marked low-pressure area formed over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal on Saturday morning concentrated into a depression by the evening.
The depression lay centred over the same region, which is about 510 km off the coast of Andaman Islands, 820 km off Vishakhapatnam coast, 910 km off Kakinada coast, 1,020 km off Machilipatnam cost and 1,100 km off Bapatla coast.
The weather system is likely to intensify into a deep depression and then gradually recurve towards the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal on Sunday. It is very likely to intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal by Monday morning, and further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal around October 27.
Thereafter, it is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach the west-central Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast around October 28. It is very likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as a very severe cyclonic storm, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115 kmph to 125 kmph, gusting to 140 kmph by October 28 noon.
Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh is bracing for the impact. The IMD has already issued a red alert for 13 districts in the State for Otober 27 and 28.
A red alert has been issued for Krishna and Bapatla districts on October 27, and for Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli, Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, NTR, Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts on October 28.
Isolated extremely heavy rainfall is expected in these districts.
The State may receive light showers on October 25 and 26, with cyclone-induced rainfall activity expected to increase from October 27.
Andhra Pradesh recorded no major rainfall activity on Saturday, with YSR Kadapa and Anantapur districts receiving widespread moderate showers. Simhadripuram in YSR Kadapa recorded 81.5 mm of rainfall between 8.30 a.m. and 5 p.m., while Malapuram in Anantapur received 74.5 mm. Other parts of Rayalaseema and south coastal Andhra Pradesh recorded light showers.
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed the officials to remain alert and take precautionary measures to deal with the situation. He called for a comprehensive plan for flood management and water conservation.

briefs.headline: 'Lie and fabrication': Iran denies Hormuz deal offer to US through Pakistan
briefs.bodyText:
Iran has denied reports that it offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its naval blockade, with the IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency saying Tehran has made no fresh proposal to Pakistani mediators.
Citing sources, Tasnim said reports by a Saudi Arabian outlet claiming that Iran had conveyed such an offer to Washington through Pakistan were “a lie and fabrication", Press TV reported.
The reports had suggested that Tehran was willing to reopen the strategic waterway if the US ended its naval blockade.
On October 18, Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi had said Tehran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days remained on the table. He made the remarks while speaking to Iranian media in Baghdad.
“Our situation is clear and based on the seven-days proposal presented to the US. They shared comments which we are reviewing… If there is any honesty on the US part, which there isn’t, the way to reopening the Strait of Hormuz is obvious,” he said.
The denial comes as US President Donald Trump has maintained that a deal with Iran remains possible, while keeping the option of further military action open. 
He has insisted that any agreement must permanently prevent Tehran from developing nuclear weapons.
Trump also threatened fresh military action against Iran if it fails to reach a diplomatic agreement with Washington, suggesting that the US could launch "another little Epic Fury".
Speaking at a campaign rally in Florida, Trump adopted a hardline stance towards Tehran, referring to previous US military action and warning that further strikes remained an option if negotiations failed.
"We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree," Trump told the cheering crowd.
Questioning Iran's willingness to negotiate, he added, "If they're smart, they'll just say, 'Let's get down to business. But, you know, I doubt they'll do that because perhaps they're not smart."
Iran claims full control over Strait of Hormuz
Amid the escalating rhetoric, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Saturday claimed that Iran retained full control over the Strait of Hormuz, adding that vessels operating in the region were being provided security in accordance with Iranian regulations.
The IRGC Navy also alleged that two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels of crude oil combined had struck naval mines while attempting to navigate a southern route through the waterway that Tehran described as unauthorised.
Iran has separately warned that it would not allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf, pushing back against Washington's claims that Iranian military capabilities had been significantly weakened.
According to Iranian state broadcaster Press TV, Major General Ali Abdollahi, chief of the general staff of Iran's armed forces, said Iranian forces had rendered the US Navy ineffective in the region.
"The US president must only dream of their military and army entering the Persian Gulf again. They will take this wish to their graves," Abdollahi said.
"We will under no circumstances and at no time allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf," he added.
Abdollahi also challenged Trump's repeated assertions that Iran's nuclear facilities had been destroyed, questioning why Washington continued to express concerns over Tehran's nuclear programme if the facilities had already been eliminated.

briefs.deck: Attack on Tiger Shroff: Weapons found in Gujarat
briefs.bodyText: Mumbai: About a week after the firing on actor-model Tiger Shroff, the Crime Branch-CID of Mumbai Police have recovered two firearms from Gujarat’s Surat. . The weapons were recovered on Friday evening following raids in Surat conducted as part of the investigation involving several states, including Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. . During the raids, two firearms and 10 cartridges were recovered. . The seized weapons and ammunition have been sent for forensic examination and ballistic testing to determine whether they match the empty shell casings found at the crime scene. .Tiger Shroff shooting: Mumbai CID seizes two firearms after Surat raids. According to Mumbai Police, the assailants fired at least five rounds at Tiger Shroff’s car. Two persons, including the driver and a vlogger, were injured in the shootout. . A motorcycle believed to have been used in the attack was later found abandoned in Andheri. . So far, Mumbai police have either arrested or detained at least 10 persons in the case.

briefs.headline: Road Ministry seeks forensic audit of its portals after vehicle data leak
briefs.deck: A senior Ministry official says they have sought the intervention of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology to review its data-sharing policy and suggest ways to strengthen it
briefs.bodyText:
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has asked the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) to conduct a forensic security audit of the VAHAN, SARATHI, e-Challan and PUCC portals, which hold various types of vehicle-owner information.
Vahan manages vehicle-registration records; Sarathi handles driving licences and related services; e-Challan records traffic violations and fines; and PUCC manages pollution control certificates.
The move follows reports of vehicle information being sold through multiple apps and websites for as little as ₹5. One Telegram-based channel, for example, provided extensive personal data when supplied with a vehicle registration number, according to an investigation by the security firm Cyderes. Details included the owner’s full name, father’s name, present and permanent addresses, PIN code, and mobile number. It also offered driving-licence details, challan history, FASTag information, a downloadable registration certificate, and a PDF of the driving licence. Vehicle Information App (with 10 million downloads) and VehicleSetu — RC & Challan Info (with 1 million downloads) were the other popular apps identified. The Ministry has now written to major app store operators, including Google, requesting the removal of all such apps.
Data-sharing policy
A senior official from the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways said they have sought the intervention of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to review its data-sharing policy and suggest ways to strengthen it. The Ministry also plans to audit various enforcement agencies accessing its portals.
The data-sharing policy allows access to data from the National Transport Repository, a central MoRTH database that consolidates vehicle-registration and driving-licence records from VAHAN and SARATHI, as well as data from e-Challans, eDARs (Detailed Accident Reports), and FASTags.
Under the policy, government bodies, including the police, law-enforcement and national-security agencies, may access all data fields available through the various applications, in accordance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Meanwhile, private entities can access only selected data fields relevant to their domain and have a daily cap on searches. Data is shared through application programming interfaces (APIs), enabling machine-to-machine access or login-based access secured by secret keys, two-factor authentication, and Aadhaar-authenticated one-time passwords (OTPs). Personally identifiable information (PII) is masked for all except law-enforcement and security agencies. All entities must possess a Security Audit Certificate from CERT-In.
Through an RTI request, the Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) found that 25,314 credentials had been issued to private entities to access VAHAN, SARATHI, e-Challan, and PUCC data, through which 1.708 crore queries were run over a period of 33 months.
According to another senior Road Ministry official, a preliminary investigation found evidence of data misuse involving the Indian government’s Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP), managed by the National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC). The finding was based on unusually high transaction volumes, with many entities permitted to access the portal recording more than 50 lakh hits in a month.
According to a letter dated October 19, reviewed by The Hindu, the Road Ministry has asked NIC to audit the access and usage patterns of entities using ULIP and determine whether they accessed data strictly in line with the approved purpose, scope, and terms of access. The Ministry has also separately written to NICDC’s data services arm to request details regarding what due diligence was carried out before granting access to entities, the criteria used to determine an entity’s eligibility, the mechanism for establishing the scope of data access (including limits placed on shared data elements), and the process followed for monitoring and reviewing data access. Officials suspect bad actors were likely triangulating data gathered from different portals and compiling it.
Road Ministry officials said that, following a representation from the IFF, the Ministry has further tightened technical controls and will limit data sharing for ULIP. Government agencies seeking data will now be required to get approval from the Transport Secretary, and requesting officers must be verified through an Aadhaar-based digital signature certificate or video KYC. However, officials ruled out suspending data sharing with private entities, saying it was necessary to support ease of doing business and ease of living.

briefs.headline: 4 years on, Mallikarjun Kharge keeps Congress afloat
briefs.deck: 4 years on, Mallikarjun Kharge keeps Congress afloat
briefs.bodyText: New Delhi: On October 26 four years ago, when Mallikarjun Kharge took over as the first non-Gandhi Congress president in 24 years, the party was in the doldrums. Its losing streak had not abated, its allies were dismissive, and the Gandhis faced a rebellion. . As he steps into the fifth year of his term on Monday, Kharge can feel satisfied that he has steadied the ship. The party has managed some impressive performances, including in the Lok Sabha, even though winning consistently against the BJP remains an unfinished assignment. . The Congress’ pre-eminent role in the Opposition has been reaffirmed during his presidency, aided by the diminishing fortunes of non-NDA regional parties. He has presided over the rollout of an organisational revamp, an idea in which Rahul Gandhi has invested quite a bit. . In a party where a section of leaders questioned Rahul’s relentless attack on the BJP-RSS and doubted the efficacy of his tactics against Hindutva, Kharge never let the attack on the Narendra Modi regime run out of steam. He remained uncompromising on secularism. . The achievements . Congress leaders acknowledge that it was Kharge’s ideological moorings that helped Rahul make social justice a core theme at a time when upper-caste leaders were circumspect about the electoral dividends of a caste census and related issues. . A highlight of Kharge’s tenure as Congress president was that he drew from the experiences of the party’s non-Gandhi chiefs, PV Narasimha Rao and Sitaram Kesri, and did not get into direct conflict with the Gandhi family, instead accepting their pre-eminent space in the Congress. .D K Shivakumar, Priyank Kharge conspiring to frame me in the sting operation: H D Kumaraswamy . At the same time, the Dalit-Buddhist leader did not lower himself to a mere rubber stamp, even as he acknowledged his limitations. His inputs were critical in decision-making, and even Rahul at times conceded to the veteran of over 60 years of political experience. . Not all decisions hit the bull’s eye. In Tamil Nadu, for instance, Kharge and other Congress seniors, including P Chidambaram, insisted on staying with the DMK. He was quick to accept a rethink after the results, by going along with the decision to join hands with C Joseph Vijay-led TVK. . Kharge also used his consensus-building skills to settle factional troubles and leadership tussles in several states like Karnataka — his home state — as well as Keralam and Punjab. . The Gandhis were particular about publicly showing respect to Kharge. His loyalty was one reason that prompted then Congress president Sonia Gandhi to lean on the veteran in 2022 after her plans to hand over the reins to Ashok Gehlot fell flat following a rebellion by MLAs supporting him. Kharge won the Congress presidential election with 7,897 votes against Shashi Tharoor’s 1,072. . Stumbling blocks . However, Kharge has a feeling that he does not get unwavering support from party leaders. He made this clear at least once, at a meeting of the Congress Working Committee. He was upset that few senior leaders backed him when he faced the “shuddikaran” ceremony in Uttarakhand in August. . He told the meeting that “good-looking people” who get considerable media space had not spoken out on the issue, even as Rahul held a press conference to demand the registration of an FIR. The party elites, his supporters feel, do not acknowledge his stature. . As recently as a week ago, Rahul highlighted Kharge’s patience and loyalty to the party to younger leaders. Since 1999, Kharge has lost the race for the Karnataka chief ministership thrice, to SM Krishna in 1999, Dharam Singh in 2004, and Siddaramaiah in 2013. Yet, he never rebelled, created trouble for the state government, or encouraged factionalism. . Humble roots . Kharge started his career as a student politician and general secretary of the students’ union at the Government Arts and Science College in present-day Kalaburagi, then known as Gulbarga. . He rose to the presidency of the Gulbarga City Congress. He was an MLA between 1972, the first time he contested, and 2009, and a minister in all Congress governments. . During the years, Kharge grew in stature to the extent that some Opposition leaders even considered him a potential prime-ministerial face ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. . A sharp political mind, Kharge was quick to dismiss such suggestions, maintaining that such decisions would be taken only after the results. . Following the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress suddenly lost momentum, witnessing electoral losses in Haryana and Maharashtra. . These were attributed to “vote chori” (vote theft), a campaign the party took up later. Kharge believes his defeat in the Gulbarga Lok Sabha seat in 2019 — his first — was the first instance of “vote chori”. . When this son of a textile-mill worker shifted to the national level after 45 years of being a major player in Karnataka politics in 2009, Delhi provided him another opportunity. At 84 years, he is still in the thick of things. . How he leads the party . As Congress president, Mallikarjun Kharge reaffirmed the party’s pre-eminent role in the Opposition; presided over the rollout of an organisational revamp championed by Rahul Gandhi; kept up sustained attacks on the Narendra Modi regime; helped Rahul make social justice a core plank of the grand old party; used his consensus-building skills to resolve factional feuds and leadership tussles in Karnataka, Keralam and Punjab; and avoided direct conflict with the Gandhi family.

stories.headline: 'Told to post it': Delhi youth arrested in ex-CM Siddaramaiah sting clip case; Bengaluru court grants 22-year-old conditional bail
stories.deck: Sleuths from the Central Crime Branch arrested a man in Delhi for a video linked to Siddaramaiah. Ritesh Pandey was brought to Bengaluru and granted conditional bail by a local court. He allegedly received instructions from a political party's social media member about the video upload. Police are investigating connections and have questioned various individuals related to the case.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Sleuths from the Central Crime Branch (CCB), Bengaluru, picked up a 22-year-old man in Delhi late Friday night in connection with the alleged sting operation involving former Karnataka chief minister 
Siddaramaiah
, marking the first arrest in the case. He was brought to Bengaluru early Saturday morning and produced in court.
A local court granted accused 
Ritesh Pandey
 conditional bail, directing him to inform the police before leaving Bengaluru and appear for questioning whenever summoned.
Police sources said Pandey uploaded the contentious video on multiple social media platforms, including a 
YouTube
 channel named ‘Karnataka Honeytrap’.
He allegedly told investigators that Prajwal Prasad, a member of a political party’s social media wing, had instructed him to upload the clip.
'Told to post clips'
According to an investigating officer, Pandey bought a used Android phone for Rs 15,000 from a shop in Delhi’s Karol Bagh market and used a USB device to upload the video. Police have recovered CCTV footage showing him buying the phone and seized a copy of the purchase bill, the officer added.
Police have also issued notices to two members of a political party’s social media team, Mohan Gowda and Chandan, seeking information about who supplied the video to Pandey. Both have been unresponsive, police sources said.
A senior IPS officer said investigators had questioned those connected with the case, including people who appeared or were heard in the video.

stories.headline: Now, one more road proposed alongside Bengaluru’s Hebbal Lake
stories.deck: The GBA has published a circulation plan for the Greater Bengaluru Local Planning Area, inviting objections and suggestions from the public. The exercise aims to expand the road network to improve traffic flow across the city.
stories.bodyText:
Even as the Bangalore Development Authority’s (BDA) Short Tunnel Project faces widespread criticism, the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has proposed another 12-metre (approximately 40-foot) road alongside Hebbal Lake in north Bengaluru as part of its draft road circulation plan.
The GBA has published a circulation plan for the Greater Bengaluru Local Planning Area, inviting objections and suggestions from the public. The exercise aims to expand the road network to improve traffic flow across the city.
The plan also proposes establishing a road link between Thanisandra and Hebbal. However, the link would also facilitate connectivity for residents of Kodigehalli and areas beyond, such as Vidyaranyapura, connecting the northern and northeastern parts of the city.
Passing on bund
The concern, however, is that the proposed route passes through the lake bund area. In addition, the same route passes alongside Nagawara Lake, essentially following the stormwater drain (SWD) network connecting the two lakes.
While experts and activists say that a road passing near a lake is not a serious concern in itself, they point out that the loss of green cover around the lake could affect the waterbody. They also warn that the proposed road would change the character of the locality and lead to commercialisation, thereby having a long-term impact on the lake. In this case, too, the area marked for the proposed road is a green space and would require tree clearance to facilitate its construction.
Priyanka Jamwal, senior fellow with the Water and Society Programme at ATREE, pointed out that the primary function of lakes was earlier irrigation. However, with changing times, lakes now largely serve as environmental amenities. “If the trees around the lake are cleared, even the function of the lake will diminish, as it would lead to massive biodiversity loss,” she said.
Further, this could affect smaller ecosystems and lead to the migration of several species. Ms. Jamwal also pointed out that lake bunds are not designed to carry heavy vehicles and that doing so would affect the buffer zone.
Recipe for destruction
V. Ramprasad, a lake activist, stressed that laying roads around lakes was a recipe for the slow destruction of waterbodies, which could eventually lead to their complete disappearance, as has happened with several other lakes in the city. “Now, they are planning a road at the site, presuming that the area is not part of the lakebed. However, what the officials forget is that the lake was initially much larger, and development has reduced its size,” he said.
Mr. Ramprasad said that, as part of the exercise, lakes where more than 10% of the lakebed area had been used for development, when assessed against lake surveys from the 1970s, should have been left untouched. He also pointed out that public opinion should have been sought before undertaking the exercise.
However, a senior GBA officer said that the draft could be reviewed and citizens could submit suggestions, based on which changes could be made.

stories.headline: Bengaluru leads post-SIR voter activity as Form 6 applications rise 32%
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Bengaluru recorded 
Karnataka
’s highest number of applications for inclusion, deletion and correction of voter details after the special intensive revision (SIR) claims deadline, even as Form 6 applications rose 32.4% and deletion requests surged 291.48% across the state.
Karnataka received 2.6 lakh Form 6 applications seeking inclusion in electoral rolls between Sept 23 and Oct 22. Form 7 applications seeking deletions or objecting to inclusions rose to 1.7 lakh, while 2.1 lakh Form 8 applications were filed for corrections and address changes, up 19.2%.
Bengaluru Urban topped Form 6 applications with 26,654, followed by Belagavi (17,437) and BBMP South (13,755), North (12,070) and Central (11,719) zones. Deletion requests were the highest in Bengaluru Urban (21,999), BBMP South (18,578) and BBMP North (17,471), followed by Dakshina Kannada (8,255) and Tumakuru (6,707).
Bengaluru Urban also led Form 8 applications with 12,255, followed by Belagavi (11,680), Dakshina Kannada (11,487), Vijayanagara (9,051) and Mysuru (9,021), according to CEO office data.
Bengaluru’s low re-entry
Bengaluru’s voter base of 1.03 crore before SIR saw a large number of electors marked absent, shifted, dead, duplicate or otherwise categorised (ASDDO) in the draft rolls. 
During the claims and objections period from Aug 24 to Sept 23, the region received only 2.2 lakh Form 6 applications for inclusion — around 5% of the ASDDO count.
The CEO’s office has not disclosed how many applicants were new voters, leaving it unclear how many excluded electors sought re-entry. Karnataka’s draft rolls recorded 1.07 crore ASDDO deletions, most of them in Bengaluru. Districts outside Bengaluru accounted for about 4 lakh deletions but submitted 5.6 lakh of the state’s 7.7 lakh Form 6 applications during the claims period.

stories.headline: Police permission sought for over 60 RSS marches across Bengaluru
stories.deck: The RSS march applications became a talking point after Home Minister Priyank Kharge took to social media to share two communications from the RSS that “informed” the police of the proposed marches in the city.
stories.bodyText:
Ahead of their Vijayadashami route marches on October 25, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) has submitted over 60 applications across the city, and the Bengaluru police are granting permissions to those that comply with standard procedures.
The RSS march applications became a talking point after Home Minister Priyank Kharge took to social media to share two communications from the RSS that “informed” the police of the proposed marches in the city. He said the RSS had to seek “permission” rather than merely “inform” the police.
Mr. Kharge stressed the need for the police to make arrangements for logistics, food, traffic management, and other requirements, as the rallies involve lakhs of participants across the State.
However, his statement drew flak, as it was seen as another face-off between Mr. Kharge and the RSS, recalling the initial denial of permission for a route march in November 2025 in the Chittapur constituency, which Mr. Kharge represents. The controversy, however, ended after the court intervened and permission was eventually granted with specific conditions.
This time, however, Mr. Kharge brought the context as he cited the Akhil Bharatiya Pratinidhi Sabha Annual Report 2025–26 to point out that over two lakh “uninformed participants” took part in more than 562 route marches in Karnataka. He said arrangements for such large gatherings were necessary; thus, prior “approval” is needed, not “information.”
Accordingly, the Bengaluru city police are now granting permissions for applications filed in accordance with the rules.
A senior police officer told The Hindu that most of the applications had been cleared for permission. “No extra or specific directions are being followed for RSS applications. Organisers have been asked to seek permission through the standard application procedure for large gatherings, and only those marches are being granted permission,” the officer said.
Police sources said applicants were directed to submit applications clearly stating the name of the organiser and at least five volunteers, along with their contact information.
“Further, they have to furnish the approximate number of participants, a route map, the reason for the marches, and the type of march.” If these details are provided, permissions are being granted,” the officer said.

briefs.headline: Ecology, flood control top residents’ priorities in blueprint for Bengaluru’s lake upkeep
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 As Bengaluru grapples with recurring floods and mounting pressure on its shrinking water bodies, residents, lake experts and environmental groups working on the rejuvenation of Halanayakanahalli lake have proposed a plan that places ecological conservation and flood mitigation above recreation and beautification.
The proposals emerged during a lake vision document (LVD) preparation exercise, supported by Wipro Foundation, Socratus, WELL Labs and Friends of Lakes. The consultation sought inputs from citizens and stakeholders on how the 42-acre, 72-gunta waterbody off Sarjapur Road should be rejuvenated in the coming years. The final LVD is expected in a few weeks.
According to volunteers associated with the initiative, the LVD exercise is being funded by Wipro Foundation, while the lake’s rejuvenation is expected to be taken up under the Centre’s Amrit Sarovar 2.0 programme. The lake has reportedly been earmarked for a project worth about Rs 9.1 crore.
Participants agreed that the waterbody’s primary role should be ecological conservation, followed by flood mitigation, groundwater recharge and rainwater harvesting, and only then community use. Discussions revealed that some participants initially prioritised recreation and community use over flood mitigation, but revised their views after experts explained the various ecological functions of urban lakes.
Among the recommendations made were limiting recreational infrastructure to 20% of the lake area, developing a 25-30ft-wide track instead of separate walking and jogging tracks, and ensuring that any sewage treatment plant at the site is restricted to 1 MLD capacity and caters only to existing inflows.
Stakeholders proposed three entrance gates serving the villages of Halanayakanahalli, Chikkanayakanahalli and Chikkannahalli, along with a separate access gate for fishermen and cattle grazers. To minimise disturbance to wildlife, participants recommended avoiding lighting within the lake premises and restricting public access after evening hours.
Manjunath, PDO of Halanayakanahalli gram panchayat, said the lake falls under minor irrigation department, which will eventually undertake development works. “We can consider the suggestions provided by citizens and NGOs on how they want their lake to look. But the LVD cannot be treated as a DPR or an official development plan,” he said.
Quote
It is very important for impacted stakeholders to engage at every stage of lake rejuvenation. It helps build a lake vision document in early stages, validate a detailed project report, review work and help monitor and maintain the lake after rejuvenation. Building a team for these activities helps in sustainable development around lakes
Chetan, Friends of Lakes

briefs.headline: Auto driver kills advocate for not accepting fare demanded for ride in Bengaluru, arrested
briefs.bodyText:
Initial suspicion of death due to heart attack turns out to be murder
Murder accused Pruthviraj Appajigowda
: Investigations into the death of a man, who was initially suspected to have died due to heart attack, have taken an intriguing turn with his autopsy revealing that he had died following a head injury caused during a fight.
The victim is Sri Ram, 43, an advocate from Kengunte. Police have now taken the accused Pruthviraj Appajigowda, 31, an auto driver from Gollarahatti in Magadi Road, into custody.
The incident took place on Oct 9 morning when Sri Ram was found lying unconscious on Nagarabavi Outer Ring Road and the on-patrol Hoysala police had shifted him to a nearby private hospital. Later on the same day, he had died.
According to police, Sri Ram never disclosed the fact that he had fallen unconscious following the fight. His family noticed injury marks on his body and approached the jurisdictional police from Annapoorneshwarinagar station, saying they suspect foul play.
The body was sent for post-mortem and the reports that recently arrived suggested that the 43-year-old advocate had died due to a blood clot in the brain.
“We learnt that Sri Ram was attacked by an auto driver near Ambedkar Institute of Technology in Mallathahalli. 
Later, we traced the auto and its driver Pruthviraj. According to Pruthviraj, there was a heated argument between the two over the tariff. Sri Ram had asked Pruthviraj for a ride and did not agree to the price quoted by him. Saying he will catch another auto, Sri Ram walked away. Angered over the refusal, Pruthviraj followed him and attacked. Sri Ram sustained internal head injuries when Pruthviraj pushed him to the ground. There were few more auto drivers with Pruthviraj when the incident took place and we are looking for them,” an investigating officer said.
“There are allegations that accused person had taken away Sri Ram’s mobile phone and some cash. We are looking into it,” he added.

briefs.headline: Cylinder explosion in RR Nagar injures three, including nine-year-old boy
briefs.deck: The incident occurred at a godown belonging to Bablu, a native of Bihar living in Bengaluru for the past 20 years, who was using the godown to store materials for his pani puri business.
briefs.bodyText:
Three people, including a nine-year-old boy, suffered injuries after a cylinder explosion at a godown in the Pattangere area of Rajarajeshwari Nagar (RR Nagar) in Bengaluru on Saturday (October 24) morning.
The injured have been identified as Bablu, Lakshmamma, who lives in a neighbouring house, and a nine-year-old boy. They were shifted to a private hospital for treatment by the police.
According to preliminary information, the incident occurred at a godown belonging to Bablu, a native of Bihar who has been living in Bengaluru for the past 20 years. Although he owns a house elsewhere, he was using the godown to store materials for his pani puri business.
A suspected gas leak from a cylinder reportedly occurred during the night, following which a fire broke out inside the godown. Pressure is believed to have built up inside the premises. When Bablu arrived in the morning and opened the door, flames suddenly burst out, injuring him and the two others.
Fire and emergency services personnel, along with the police, inspected the spot. Further details about the cause of the incident and the extent of the injuries are awaited.

stories.headline: Anthropic PB admits to having an Indian subsidiary, contradicts earlier stand in court
stories.deck: This violates corporate ethics, says founder of Belagavi-based company who has filed the complaint
stories.bodyText:
A legal dispute over the use of the name ‘Anthropic’ has taken a new turn after US-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic PBC acknowledged in the Belagavi Commercial Court that a wholly owned subsidiary operates in India.
Belagavi-based Anthropic Softwares Private Limited has claimed to have registered the name of the company and brand much before the US-based firm, and has challenged the use of the company’s name by the American entity.
“In a written statement filed in the court, the company stated that Irina Ghose is the managing director of the India entity. This development raises questions about corporate conduct and the positions taken during the proceedings,” said Mohammad Ayyaz Mulla, Managing Director of Belagavi-based Anthropic Softwares Private Limited.
“For over 10 months, Anthropic India Private Limited resisted being impleaded in the case, maintaining that it was a separate legal entity and disputing the existence of a cause of action against it. More significantly, in an objection supported by an affidavit on oath, its Managing Director, Irina Ghose, denied that Anthropic India was directly or indirectly promoting Anthropic PBC’s business, calling the allegation baseless and requiring strict proof.
“Anthropic PBC’s subsequent written statement refers to its wholly owned Indian subsidiary and identifies Ms. Ghose as its managing director. We want to ask whether these positions, considered together, reflected the transparency and professional ethics expected of a global technology company. He said the court should examine whether procedural objections were being used to delay consideration of the core dispute over prior use of the ‘Anthropic’ name.”
Mr. Mulla alleged that repeated misdirected emails intended for Anthropic PBC had reached his company despite regular notifications, creating business disruption, brand confusion, and potential data-security risk, including the possibility of sensitive communications reaching unintended recipients. He said the continuing problem raised serious questions about whether customer confidentiality and corrective action were receiving adequate attention. He urged the US company to demonstrate its belief in corporate ethics through its behaviour.

stories.headline: IDFC First Bank Q2 profit nearly triples to Rs 1,045 crore; loan assets rise 30%
stories.deck: In Q2 FY27, IDFC First Bank showcased an impressive profit surge of 196.5 percent year-on-year, reaching Rs 1,045 crore. The bank's robust core operating performance is highlighted by a 21 percent rise in net interest income. Additionally, total loan assets expanded by 30.1 percent, showcasing substantial business growth. With gross non-performing assets reduced to 1.32 percent, management…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: IDFC First Bank reported a 196.5 per cent year-on-year jump in profit after tax to Rs 1,045 crore in the September quarter of FY27, supported by strong growth in core operating profit and an improvement in asset quality.
Core operating profit, excluding trading gains, rose 38.5 per cent to Rs 2,527 crore. Net interest income (NII) increased 21 per cent to Rs 6,184 crore, while fee and other income grew 24.5 per cent to Rs 2,285 crore.
Total loan assets, including credit substitutes and loans backed by foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR(B)) deposits, rose 30.1 per cent year-on-year to Rs 3,46,913 crore as of September 30, 2026. Excluding FCNR(B)-backed loans, growth stood at 22.2 per cent on a gross basis, including inter-bank participation certificates (IBPC).
Total deposits increased 25.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 3,48,583 crore. The bank mobilised Rs 34,390 crore in FCNR(B) deposits during the quarter, taking advantage of its digital capabilities despite having no branch, subsidiary or representative office outside India.
The bank said the FCNR(B) deposits, largely carrying tenures of three to five years, would provide structural liquidity in the coming years. Their fully loaded cost, including priority sector lending benefits, is approximately 1 per cent lower than the cost of raising domestic fixed deposits.
The bank's average current account and savings account (CASA) ratio stood at 48.4 per cent during the quarter, compared with 50.1 per cent in the preceding quarter. Management attributed the decline primarily to the large mobilisation of FCNR(B) deposits.
Asset quality improved, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 1.32 per cent from 1.86 per cent a year earlier. Net NPA stood at 0.40 per cent, against 0.53 per cent in the year-ago period. Credit cost, as a percentage of average assets, declined to 1.01 per cent in Q2 FY27.
The bank's return on assets (RoA) stood at 0.93 per cent for the quarter, while core RoA improved to 0.92 per cent from 0.88 per cent in the June quarter, excluding interest received on an income tax refund in Q1 FY27.
Management said operating expenses had grown more slowly than income by over 500 basis points year-on-year for two consecutive quarters. The core cost-to-income ratio improved to 70.16 per cent in Q2 FY27 from 70.73 per cent in the preceding quarter.
The bank also said the benefits of FCNR(B) deposit mobilisation, cost savings, product changes and expected repo rate increases could broadly offset the anticipated impact of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India's consultation paper on insurance commissions on profitability in FY28.

stories.headline: AU Small Finance Bank Q2 profit jumps 53% to 858 crore

AU Small Finance Bank on Saturday (October 24, 2026) reported a 53% surge in net profit at ₹858 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026 on the back of improvement in interest income. The lender had earned a net profit of ₹561 crore in the year-ago period.
“Total income rose to ₹6,382 crore in the quarter under review from ₹5,224 crore in the same period a year ago,” AU Small Finance Bank said in a regulatory filing. Interest income increased to ₹5,612 crore as against ₹4,511 crore in the corresponding second quarter of the previous year.
Net interest income of the bank improved to ₹2,820 crore in the July-September quarter, from ₹2,144 crore in the September quarter of 2025, registering a growth of 32%. Net interest margin increased to 5.8% from 5.5% at the end of September 2025.

Net NPAs or bad loan too moderated to 0.81%, as against 0.88% in the year-ago period. However, the Capital Adequacy Ratio of the bank decreased to 18.54%, from 18.78% at the end of September 2025.
"This quarter's performance is a reflection of the institution we are steadily building, one that combines growth with profitability, and ambition with prudence," AU Small Finance Bank MD & CEO Sanjay Agarwal said.
“The balanced growth of the franchise, improving profitability and stable asset quality reinforce confidence that the foundations for sustained, long-term performance are firmly in place,” he added.

stories.headline: Kotak Mahindra Bank Q2 results: Consolidated net profit jumps 26% to Rs 5,645 crore
stories.deck: Kotak Mahindra Bank reported an impressive 26% growth in its consolidated net profit for the September quarter of FY27. Standalone profit surged by 29%, reaching Rs 4,212 crore. The bank's asset quality improved, as evidenced by the notable decrease in gross non-performing assets. Moreover, the net interest income increased by 16%, with a robust capital adequacy ratio of 21.9%. Nevertheless, the…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Kotak Mahindra Bank on Saturday reported a 26 per cent increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 5,645 crore for the September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 4,468 crore in the same period last year, as higher income and a decline in provisions supported earnings.
The private sector lender's standalone net profit rose 29 per cent year-on-year to Rs 4,212 crore from Rs 3,253 crore.
The bank also reported an improvement in asset quality during the quarter. Its gross non-performing assets (GNPA) ratio declined to 1.04 per cent from 1.39 per cent a year earlier, while the net NPA ratio fell to 0.24 per cent from 0.32 per cent.
Fresh loan slippages decreased to Rs 1,230 crore from Rs 1,629 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Provisions and contingencies were also lower, falling 15 per cent to Rs 803 crore.
Additionally, it reported that its net interest income (NII) increased 16 per cent to Rs 8,459 crore from Rs 7,311 crore a year ago. Operating profit climbed 21 per cent to Rs 6,382 crore, while fees and services income grew 21 per cent to Rs 2,926 crore.
The bank recorded a 25 per cent rise in net advances to Rs 5,77,295 crore as of September 30, 2026. 
Total deposits increased 23 per cent to Rs 6,51,491 crore.
However, a significant part of this growth was linked to funds mobilised through the Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) scheme. Excluding FCNR(B)-related loans and the portfolio acquired from Kotak Mahindra Investments, advances grew 19 per cent. Deposit growth stood at 13 per cent after excluding FCNR(B) deposits.
Despite the increase in income, the bank witnessed pressure on its lending margins. Net interest margin (NIM) declined to 4.31 per cent from 4.54 per cent in the year-ago quarter and 4.53 per cent in the preceding quarter.
The bank attributed the moderation largely to the mobilisation of around Rs 55,344 crore in FCNR(B) deposits under the Reserve Bank of India's concessional swap facility. It also disbursed loans worth approximately Rs 16,110 crore through its international branches under the arrangement.
The inflows affected the bank's deposit mix, with its current account and savings account (CASA) ratio falling to 38.2 per cent from 42.3 per cent a year earlier. Excluding FCNR(B) deposits, the ratio stood at 41.8 per cent.
Managing director and CEO Ashok Vaswani said the bank expects its net interest margins to remain stable during the rest of the financial year. While the deployment of funds raised through the FCNR(B) scheme could weigh on margins, the impact is expected to be offset by RBI rate hikes, given that around 60 per cent of the bank's loan book is linked to the repo rate.
The bank's capital adequacy ratio stood at 21.9 per cent as of September 30, 2026, with its Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio at 21.4 per cent.

briefs.headline: Ultra Gas targeting to add 15 LNG retail stations by end of fiscal: CEO
briefs.deck: Speaking to The Hindu, Maqsood Shaikh, CEO and Managing Director of Ultra Gas, emphasised that a dedicated policy for LNG-based transportation is an imperative for the fuel segment to grow.
briefs.bodyText:
Ultra Gas, the Essar-backed green fuel retailer, plans to add 15 retail stations for liquefied natural gas (LNG) used in vehicles by the end of the current financial year, taking its network to 25, Maqsood Shaikh, chief executive officer and managing director, told The Hindu on Thursday.
The company aims to expand its network to more than 100 outlets by the end of FY29, entailing an investment of ₹900 crore.
The expansion is expected to improve refuelling access for long-haul freight operators and encourage the adoption of LNG-fuelled trucks. With 25 stations operational by March, the company expects refuelling facilities to be available every 200-250 km across its network.
“With the 25 stations expected by the end of March, there would be 98% assurance that refuelling stations would be available in a span of [every] 200 to 250 kilometres,” Mr. Shaikh said.
The network expansion could generate demand for around 6,000 LNG-fuelled trucks, he added.
Cost advantage
Mr. Shaikh said LNG-powered freight transportation could deliver fuel-cost savings of 25-30% compared with diesel-powered trucks, combining better fuel efficiency with lower fuel prices.
“LNG-fuelled trucks would help augur 25%-30% more savings than diesel. 15% would be because of its standalone fuel efficiency during combustion and the rest because of 10-15% discounting to diesel,” he said.
Ultra Gas is replicating an outlet design that has already received approval and support from the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO). A recent amendment to the Static and Mobile Pressure Vessels (Unfired) Rules, removing the requirement for a no-objection certificate from the district magistrate, is also expected to accelerate the establishment of new stations, according to him.
Call for dedicated policy
Mr. Shaikh stressed that a dedicated LNG policy was essential to address uncertainty among transporters, lenders and investors.
“Today fund managers and bankers are not wanting to sponsor LNG trucking projects because they are not sure about the government’s viewpoint on the adoption of the fuel. It suffers the lacuna of being overshadowed by electric mobility,” he said.
He also emphasised the need for long-term LNG procurement agreements rather than reliance on spot purchases. Ultra Gas currently has five-to-10-year supply agreements with GAIL, Indian Oil, Shell and Hindustan Petroleum.

briefs.headline: Ethanol tender sparks feedstock concerns as rice gains ground over maize
briefs.deck: The competing concerns highlight the challenge facing the ethanol procurement framework: balancing the availability and cost of different feedstocks.
briefs.bodyText:
The Oil Marketing Companies’ (OMCs) latest ethanol procurement tender for Ethanol Supply Year (ESY) 2026–27 has triggered concerns among grain-based ethanol producers and sections of the sugar industry over feedstock pricing, allocation priorities and the potential implications for the sector.
The tender sets procurement prices at ₹60.32 a litre for surplus foodgrains (SFG), with a stated cap of 108 crore litres for the first three quarters; ₹64 a litre for damaged foodgrains (DFG); and ₹66 a litre for maize, plus an additional ₹2.79 a litre. While ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses has been excluded, C-heavy molasses-based ethanol remains eligible for procurement.
Rice-based ethanol in focus
The Grain Ethanol Manufacturers Association (GEMA) has argued that the tender places a disproportionate burden on rice-based feedstocks, particularly SFG and DFG, while potentially weakening maize’s role as an industrial feedstock.
The pricing differential has also created uncertainty over how procurement demand will be distributed among the different feedstock categories.
According to industry estimates, DFG-based ethanol allocation during ESY 2025–26 was approximately 60 crore litres. For ESY 2026–27, the industry anticipates that the allocation could exceed 700 crore litres.
C.K. Jain, president of GEMA, said a balanced ethanol policy must support viable production from both maize and rice, with procurement prices reflecting their different cost structures and allocations providing reasonable visibility to producers. He added that the government and OMCs should review the pricing and allocation framework.
GEMA has also questioned whether maize will receive adequate procurement opportunities under the lowest-price-based allocation mechanism. It has called for greater clarity on the methodology for feedstock-wise allocation and the role envisaged for maize in meeting the country’s ethanol requirements.
Sugar industry welcomes curbs, flags allocation preference
The Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) has welcomed the exclusion of ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses, arguing that the approach is consistent with the need to safeguard domestic sugar availability amid uncertainty over the forthcoming crop.
C-heavy molasses-based ethanol, it noted, allows sugar mills to continue contributing to the ethanol-blending programme without diverting recoverable sugar.
However, ISMA has raised concerns over the preferential allocation granted to dedicated ethanol plants holding Long-Term Offtake Agreements under the ESY 2026–27 tender.
While the provision is already in place for the current year, its continuation in subsequent years could hurt the sugar industry, the association said.

briefs.headline: Data suggests broad-based increase in food prices: RBI Bulletin
briefs.deck: Inflation in rural areas was found to be higher than in urban areas; headline CPI inflation edged up over the months and showed signs of greater generalisation across commodities
briefs.bodyText:
High-frequency data collected by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for October (till 19th), suggest a broad-based increase in food prices, said RBI officials in the October edition of RBI Bulletin, which was released on Friday (October 23, 2026).
“Among cereals, rice and wheat prices continued to increase. Prices of major pulses also went up sequentially. Edible oil prices also recorded a slow and broad-based increase, led by mustard and palm oil,” they wrote in the ‘State of the Economy’ article.
Among vegetables, while potato prices declined and the pace of onion price increases dropped, tomato prices picked up, they added.
Surprisingly, inflation in rural areas has been getting higher than that in urban areas. Inflation stood at 4.9% and 6.1%, respectively, in urban and rural areas in September. In August, urban and rural inflation stood at 4.3% and 5.2% respectively, the officials stated.
The majority of States/UTs recorded inflation in the range of 4-6% in September. Inflation ranged from 2.9% to 6.9% across states/UTs. States like Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry recorded inflation in excess of 6% across both rural and urban areas, they pointed out.
Stating that WPI inflation recorded its first double-digit rate in the new series (Base 2022-23) at 11.4% in September 2026, rising from 9.9% in August, reflecting a broad-based increase in prices, they said industrial and farm input costs remained elevated.
Inflation in the Output Producer Price Index surged to 11.4% in September 2026 from 9.8% in August, led by manufacturing products, and mining & quarrying, they said.
As per the article headline, CPI inflation edged up over the months and showed signs of greater generalisation across commodities, calling for a commensurate change in the monetary policy stance.
“The external headwinds are also being dealt with a slew of regulatory measures by the Reserve Bank to curb speculative activity in foreign exchange market,” they stated.
“Strong inflows under FCNR(B) swap window augmented reserves. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) and remittance flows strengthened in August. With strong exports growth, the trade deficit narrowed in September,” they added.
The headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation rose to a 23-month high of 5.5% (YoY) in September from 4.8% in August, driven by a broad-based increase in food, fuel and core (CPI excluding food and fuel) components.
Eleven out of twelve divisions witnessed a sequential increase in inflation, they said.
Despite the West Asia conflict having entered its eighth month, keeping energy prices elevated and supply chains constrained, causing uncertainties in trade policies and volatility in financial markets, the Indian economy has withstood the shocks well, the officials wrote.
“The IMF raised India’s growth projection for 2026-27 by 60 basis points [bps] to 7%, from its July estimate, citing stronger-than-expected momentum, driven by resilient domestic demand and robust services activity. The high-frequency indicators maintained their upward trajectory,” they stated.
Emphasising that the Indian economy has been anchored by solid macroeconomic fundamentals and policy interventions to cushion downside risks, they said that despite being a net energy importer, its GDP growth has been supported by sustained domestic demand and services.

briefs.headline: Commerce Ministry identifying AI-proof professions, sectors where India can take global lead: Goyal
briefs.deck: The Commerce and Industry Minister said that the focus would be on sectors where AI could improve efficiency without necessarily replacing human workers, while leveraging India’s large pool of skilled talent, youthful population and traditional strengths
briefs.bodyText:
The Commerce Ministry is identifying professions that are less vulnerable to artificial intelligence (AI) to prepare for the fast-changing technological landscape and tap opportunities for India to emerge as a global leader, Union Minister Piyush Goyal has said.
The Commerce and Industry Minister said that the focus would be on sectors where AI could improve efficiency without necessarily replacing human workers, while leveraging India's large pool of skilled talent, youthful population and traditional strengths.
"I got my Ministry to start working on what are the AI-proof professions. After all, we have to plan as a nation for so many millions of people. What are the sectors where AI can at max add to efficiency, not necessarily replace (human workforce)," the Minister said on Friday (October 23, 2026) while addressing Indian science and technology researchers and students in Germany.
When asked about the objective of the initiative, he said India could take global leadership in several areas, including handicrafts, handloom, culinary arts and tourism, leveraging its vast pool of skilled talent and youthful population.
In these sectors, traditional skills and human creativity remain important, he said.
"... our handicraft, handloom... no amount of AI can replace that. So there are many, many areas where I think we have some very special strengths which we will be focusing on, also simultaneously developing, to ensure that 1.4 billion people have a better life in the future," he added.
Asked whether the government planned to offer incentives to these sectors, Mr. Goyal said support would be provided wherever necessary, but incentives would not be required for every activity.
"It'll be a mix of several initiatives, some privately led, some government led, some people led, some opportunity led," he said, adding the broader objective was to develop India's strengths and create opportunities that would help improve the lives of its 1.4 billion people.
Mr. Goyal also talked about exploring ways to attract Indian researchers, engineers, and scientists working abroad to return and contribute to the country's development.
"I've asked them (the researchers and students here) to tell us what they will need to consider (the idea) and how we can support more, young researchers or our talented engineers and scientific community to come and work and serve in India," he said.
Mr. Goyal said his discussions had highlighted that attracting talent was not merely a question of financial incentives, but also of creating a supportive environment for research and innovation.
"And surprisingly, I realise it's not just about money; it's about the enabling environment, the support of the ecosystem. So I (will) talk to my colleagues in the government, with educational institutions, both in the government and private sector, with academia, with leading research institutions in India, and industry, to see how we can forge industry, academia, and researchers partnerships," he said.
Referring to future global growth prospects, Mr. Goyal said developed countries would increasingly need to engage with emerging economies in Asia, Africa and Latin America, as these regions would drive future growth.
There are about 3,30,000 people of Indian origin in Germany, plus nearly 60-70,000 students.
"This large Indian student community, full of enthusiasm, seems to be very excited about taking their learnings back to India. Now we can see them not just looking for a job in Germany, but wanting to be back home to contribute to the India growth story, because that is where the action is," Mr. Goyal told reporters.
The Minister was here to discuss ways with government and private sector leaders to boost trade and investment between India and Germany.
