briefs.headline: From fuel price hikes to cost-of-living concerns, US consumer sentiment nears record low
briefs.deck: US consumer sentiment has declined slightly as rising prices related to the Middle East conflict affect households' financial views. The Consumer Sentiment Index fell marginally to 48.0 in October, approaching a record low. Independents reported significantly weaker sentiment while Democrats and Republicans showed improvements. Inflation expectations rose, suggesting concerns about future price…
briefs.bodyText:
US consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices linked to the Middle East conflict weighed on households' views of the economy, a University of Michigan survey showed on Friday, with affordability emerging as a key issue ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
The university's Consumer Sentiment Index slipped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected a reading of 46.3, which was also the preliminary estimate for October.
October's reading was the second-lowest on record, following the all-time low of 44.8 recorded in May, shortly after the Iran war began.
"Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy," said Joanne Hsu, director of the Surveys of Consumers. "Sentiment is now 10% below a year ago and 15% less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict."
Independent voters report weaker sentiment
The survey's findings coincided with political polling showing that voters held a dim view of the economy and President Donald Trump's and the Republican Party's handling of it, Reuters reported.
Millions of Americans have already cast early ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress for the final two years of Trump's term.
Polls indicated Republicans were likely to lose control of the House of Representatives, with the Senate also potentially at stake. Trump's approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll stood at a record low, amid a surge in fuel prices following his decision to attack Iran in late February.
The University of Michigan survey found that the decline in sentiment was driven by respondents who identified as independents, a group that includes swing voters.
Their sentiment score fell to 42.4 in October from 47.7 in September, putting it just above May's record low of 40.6. Sentiment scores among Democrats and Republicans improved.
The survey also found that more independents and Republicans were citing high prices as a strain on their personal finances. Since January, the number of independents reporting inflation pressures as a financial burden had risen by 27%, while the figure among Republicans had increased by 52%. Among Democrats, the increase was 15%.
Households with little or no exposure to the stock market had also increasingly cited high prices as a financial burden compared with the beginning of the year. The stock market had recently climbed rapidly amid enthusiasm for investments in artificial intelligence.
Inflation expectations remain elevated
The survey's measure of consumers' expectations for inflation over the next 12 months rose to 4.7% in October from 4.6% in September. The measure had stood at 3.4% in February, before the US-Israeli war with Iran began.
Expectations for inflation over the next five years increased to 3.5% from 3.4% in September and 3.2% in March, shortly after the conflict began.
In an accompanying report, Hsu said persistently elevated inflation expectations in the period following the Covid-19 pandemic posed a risk to the Federal Reserve's efforts to bring inflation down to its 2% target. The target had remained unmet for more than five years, she wrote.
"Consumers broadly expect inflation to accelerate, and this year’s increases in inflation expectations are not limited to one part of the political spectrum," Hsu said.
She also cautioned that relatively resilient consumer spending, despite negative views of the economy, required close attention. If households were spending now to avoid expected price increases in the future, bringing inflation down could become more difficult, she added.
Federal Reserve decision due next week
Federal Reserve officials are scheduled to meet in Washington next week. Despite recent inflation readings that came in higher than expected, they were broadly expected to keep the policy interest rate unchanged at 3.75%-4.00%.
The Fed had raised the rate by a quarter of a percentage point in September. Most officials had indicated a need for higher interest rates, while key policymakers had also expressed willingness to wait for more data before making their next move.

stories.headline: My father pushes me to become a better player, says Tagenarine
stories.bodyText:
Every time Tagenarine Chanderpaul makes his way into the middle, he carries the weight of a surname that is etched in cricket fanatics’ hearts.
No day on the pitch passes by without the mention of his father Shivnarine Chanderpaul, a legendary figure in the world game. Unfortunately for the West Indies opener, he has not kicked on in his Test career after entering the international arena with promise.
Four years into his journey with the Men in Maroon, Tagenarine has come to terms with the constant comparisons with his dad but is striving to create a name for himself.
“Wherever I go, people expect me to perform as good as him. But I cannot be him, I can only be myself,” the 30-year-old told The Hindu recently. “He was a great player, but I just try to be myself. As an individual, I do the best I can.”
While Tagenarine wades through challenges, Shivnarine, as both a father and mentor, attempts to make the former’s path easier.
“He shares his knowledge and experience to make me a better player. He is a very competitive and serious guy. He keeps pushing me to get better,” said the southpaw.
Tagenarine, lucky enough to be taught a masterclass on a regular basis, knows where he is lacking: he has just one ton and two half-centuries in 15 long-format matches (758 runs). “I need to be more consistent, convert starts into big scores. Sometimes, you get comfortable in the middle and get out. But Test cricket is tough... there is no time to relax,” the top-order batter added.
His stint at the Super Kings Academy — in the company of West Indies red-ball teammates — may be the launchpad for bigger things ahead. “I always believe in putting in the work, so hopefully I can reap the rewards of it”.

stories.headline: Indian Super League: Ajaraie misses last-gasp penalty as Odisha hold NEUFC
stories.bodyText:
KOLKATA: It was almost an encore of their 
Indian Super League
 opener as NorthEast United once again looked set for a very late win on Saturday as Odisha FC defender Stephen Eze conceded a penalty in the fifth minute of injury time.
However, contrary to expectations, Alaaeddine Ajaraie’s spot kick beat goalkeeper Hrithik Tiwary but not the woodwork as the match at Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar ended in a goalless draw.
It was, in fact, a fair result for the eighth-paced Juggernauts, who got their first point of the season, and their impressive defence, as the Highlanders failed to continue their winning run even as the point took them to the top of the table with seven points from three matches.
The match began as a tactical battle between the coaches with TS Purushothaman resorting to a strong defensive shape that the hosts have been more used to over the seasons, with three centre-backs – Jeremy Zohminghlua, veteran Eze and Thoiba Singh Moirangthem – inside the six-yard box.
It was a perfect answer to Juan Pedro Benali’s tactic of quick attack with Ajaraie in a more central role in combination with Nikola Ninkovic and aided by Jithin MS and Macarton Nickson from the wings.
Jithin, who scored the winner in their opener against the mighty Mohun Bagan Super Giant, created the first NEUFC attack as early as in the third minute with a run from the right wing and beating a persistent Jeremy to send in a ball at the centre. But Odisha’s young custodian Hrithik Tiwary stood tall to parry the shot from Ninkovic towards safety.
Ajaraie, away from his conventional position in the flanks, made a few impressive runs throughout the first half, especially in the 23rd and 28th minutes, down the middle, but after dodging and nutmegging the defenders, failed to produce the finish that his Spanish coach hoped for from the sidelines.
Odisha, on the other hand, depended on counter-attacks as Everton Nascimento, Mahmoud Eid and K Lalrinfela waited in the opposition half to find a breakthrough.
The best chance of the half came to Antonio Moyano in the 45th minute but, with only Tiwary to beat, he shot the ball too high to make a difference.
Although devoid of a goal, the match continued to be an exciting affair with a proactive Jithin and skilful Ajaraie used all tricks in their bag to get past the Odisha defence. There were also physical duels, like the ones involving the young Blue Tigers and Highlanders attacker Pramveer Singh and Odisha skipper Lalthathanga Khawlhring or ‘Putieia’ in the middle.
However, the scoreline stayed unchanged even as the ends were changed and both coaches brought in reinforcements.
Even as the NEUFC attacks continued, with Ajaraie and Ninkovic coming very close to scoring throughout the second half, Everton and Eid combined near the NEUFC goal with some impressive moves, together with substitute Rahim Ali, only for the hard-working Nikhil Barla at the back and Gurmeet Singh in goal coming to NEUFC’s rescue.
That was until the 95th minute of the match when all the hard work from Odisha looked to have been put paid by the outstretched hand of Eze inside the box.
However, it was not to be as the right post saved Ajaraie’s penalty kick and Odisha’s day in front of the home crowd.

briefs.headline: For record-breaking Chuki, this is just the start of big things
briefs.bodyText:
It all started with an ‘enough is enough, full stop’. Then came a punishment at school, and now, a national record.
For 19-year-old Chuki Birda of Rajasthan, a couple of deep breaths, a glance at the board displaying the national record mark and one final look at the crossbar preceded her sprint down the runway.
Seconds later, she cleared the bar and landed in the pit, setting a new national record with 3.91m in the pole vault at the 41st National Junior Athletics Championships at the Nehru Stadium here on Saturday.
A handful of vociferous supporters from her village, along with well-wishers from Chennai, screamed in delight from the stands.
The name ‘Chuki’, according to her mentor Ram Nivas Sahu, means ‘full stop’ in the local dialect. She is one of eight daughters. Her parents gave her the name in the belief that the next child would be a boy. But the next two were girls too.
It was a punishment at school that first brought her sporting ability to notice.
“She was asked to run, touch a wall and return to the classroom. Chuki came first, and that was when I noticed her speed,” recalled Ram Nivas, her mentor and a government school teacher.
Chuki initially played kabaddi before moving to running and hurdles, and eventually took up pole vault.
“We didn’t know anything about pole vault. We watched videos on YouTube and started learning the basics,” said Ram Nivas.
Help arrived through his former classmate Nidhi Chaudhari, an IAS officer, and the Mumbai-based Parmarth Seva Samiti, which, according to him, provided equipment worth ₹10 lakh.
Chuki now trains in Haryana under Captain Ramdari Singh.
“Our coach spends the whole day with us. He takes care of everything, including injuries,” said Chuki. “I suffered injuries two or three times. It has taken me a long time to reach 3.91m,” added the 19-year-old.
Coming from a farming family, Chuki credits her parents for standing by her. “My father supports me, but my mother supports me even more,” she said, adding that she hopes to do well at the senior level next year.
“She will win an international medal for India,” said Ram Nivas.
For a journey that began with a ‘full stop’, Chuki’s story, it seems, is only just beginning.

briefs.headline: Arsenal sink Everton to join Manchester City at Premier League summit
briefs.deck: Ezri Konsa bundled the ball into the net in the opening minutes for his first goal for the club since joining from Aston Villa in August
briefs.bodyText:
Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 on Saturday (October 24, 2026) to pull level with Manchester City at the top of the Premier League, rediscovering their taste for set-piece goals at a rainswept Emirates.
Ezri Konsa bundled the ball into the net in the opening minutes for his first goal for the club since joining from Aston Villa in August.
Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the home side's lead midway through the second period.
The win meant Arsenal took full advantage of City's 2-1 defeat at Villa Park in Saturday's (October 24) kick-off -- the first time Enzo Maresca's men had dropped points this season.
Both teams are now on 21 points, but City, the Gunners' main title rivals in recent seasons, have a superior goal difference.
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta was forced to shuffle his pack after Bukayo Saka suffered a muscle injury in the midweek Champions League draw at Bayern Munich, picking Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze as his wide players.
Arteta was already short of wingers, with Christos Tzolis still sidelined and both Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard sold during the summer transfer window.
The home team started strongly and took the lead in the seventh minute after their third corner, following a scramble in the box.
Martin Odegaard's inswinging delivery was flicked on by Gabriel. Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford got his fingertips to the bouncing ball but it fell to Konsa, who poked it home at the back post.
Set-piece kings
It was the first non-penalty set-piece goal in all competitions in the current campaign for Arsenal -- who earned a reputation last season as set-piece kings as they won their first Premier League title in a generation.
Everton responded positively. Tyrique George's shot was deflected behind by Ben White but Arsenal were largely in control.
Madueke, recently deemed surplus to requirements by the watching England boss Thomas Tuchel, impressed on the right wing, spinning and hitting the side netting on the half-hour mark.
Arsenal had a major scare as the clock ticked towards half-time when a careless header from Ben White back to his goalkeeper David Raya was intercepted by Thierno Barry, but the Everton forward was unable to make clean contact and Raya made the save.
Gunners midfielder Mikel Merino flashed a header over the bar in the closing moments of the half, which ended with 13 shots and 10 corners for the home side, but just the solitary goal.
Gabriel went down in pain 10 minutes after the restart, stretching to intercept the ball, but was able to resume after treatment on the pitch.
Arteta made a triple substitution in the 68th minute, bringing on Kai Havertz, Bruno Guimaraes and Riccardo Calafiori.
Moments later they were 2-0 ahead when Gabriel rose to head home White's cross after a neatly worked move down the right.
Teenager Max Dowman, who became the youngest-ever Premier League goalscorer in the same fixture last season, was introduced for the final 10 minutes.
Everton almost pulled a goal back when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall flashed a header just wide of Raya's post but that was the last major scare on a satisfactory day for Arsenal.

briefs.headline: No Virat Kohli in Rahane's all-time India Test XI; picks Dravid, Sachin & Dhoni
briefs.deck: Rahane, 38, named MS Dhoni as captain and wicketkeeper, explaining that the former India skipper was his first captain in international cricket.
briefs.bodyText:
Virat Kohli
 and 
Rohit Sharma
 were missing from former India batter 
Ajinkya Rahane
's all-time India Test XI, which features only players he has played alongside in international or domestic cricket.
Rahane, 38, named MS Dhoni as captain and wicketkeeper, explaining that the former India skipper was his first captain in international cricket. He picked Murali Vijay and Shikhar Dhawan as openers, followed by Rahul Dravid at No. 3 and Sachin Tendulkar at No. 4.
Rahane selected himself at No. 5, with Dhoni batting at No. 6. Ravindra Jadeja and Ravichandran Ashwin were his all-round and spin-bowling options, while Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Mohammed Shami and Ishant Sharma made up the pace attack. The three fast bowlers were part of the Indian team that ushered in a pace-focused era in 2018 and helped secure several memorable Test wins overseas.
Kohli and Rohit, two of India's leading batters in recent years, did not make the cut.
Rahane retired from all forms of cricket in July this year. The right-handed batter announced his decision through an emotional video on social media.
He was dropped from India's Test team after the two-match away series against the West Indies in 2023. Rahane scored eight runs in his final innings in international cricket.
He finished his Test career with 5,077 runs from 85 matches at an average of 38.46. He also played 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is, scoring 2,962 and 375 runs, respectively.

briefs.headline: Dominant India aims to seal ODI series against Zimbabwe
briefs.bodyText:
The sun will rise in the east. A day has 24 hours. India will beat Zimbabwe. Some certainties are written into the fabric of the universe. This one comes stamped with a scoreboard.
None of this is meant as a disrespect. Even the visitor speaks of an upset as a miracle: improbable, yet gloriously welcome should it arrive. But miracles demand fresh legs, and Zimbabwe’s are running on fumes. They come into the second ODI at the BCA Stadium in Kotambi on Sunday carrying the bruises of a nine-wicket loss and the weight of a calendar that has given them little mercy.
The Lady Chevrons have been the busiest side in international cricket recently, playing non-stop since September. Niggles have crept up, with Josephine Nkomo and Kelis Ndhlovu missing the 1st ODI. Recovery has been a challenge, with the priority for the camp being the ICC Emerging Nations Trophy, which gets underway in Bangkok in November.
India, meanwhile, eyes an unassailable lead but isn’t without its own headaches.
The pacers were erratic in the 1st ODI. Nandani Sharma, who made way for debutant Jintimani Kalita, was spotted doing her routines with her left knee in a compression brace. But the bigger issues are the wayward lines India settled into after the PowerPlay and an inability to bowl to set fields, which Zimbabwe smartly capitalised on.
Will India be brave and give wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh, whose errors have been piling up, a rest to allow Baroda girl Yastika Bhatia, who graces several billboards around the venue, a spot in the side? Or is there room for both, the way India has managed to embrace Shafali Verma and Pratika Rawal?
Coach Amol Muzumdar and captain Smriti Mandhana must weigh rotating players to build depth for the South Africa tour or stick with a winning lineup.

briefs.headline: Vaisakh Chandran corrects bowling action, regains his rhythm
briefs.bodyText:
The last two seasons were forgettable for off-spinner Vaisakh Chandran. A finger injury, followed by a shoulder injury, sidelined him. In between, he lost his bowling action and, consequently, his wicket-taking ability. The Ranji Trophy match against Karnataka at the KCA Stadium in Mangalapuram last season was particularly chastening; he was savaged by Karun Nair and R. Smaran, conceding over 100 runs at nearly five runs an over. His shoulder injury then flared up, forcing him to spend the rest of the season in rehabilitation.
“I knew something was wrong but I was helpless. I was just going through the motions in the match against Karnataka. The shoulder was hurting as well. I felt a sharp pain on my right shoulder whenever I threw the ball while fielding. I think I over-bowled in the nets. I was told to bowl 30 overs daily during practice by our former coach and I followed it. The pain worsened, forcing me to consult a doctor who advised rest,”
During his rehabilitation, he watched the video of the Karnataka match and compared them with old footage and realised his bowling action had changed drastically.
“I went back to the drawing board, worked on my action. I also sought the help of Biju George, who pointed out the flaws and helped me to correct them,” he said.
“It is a common problem for all bowlers to lose their original action when they play a lot. Every bowler has a specific arm slot from which he delivers the ball comfortably. In Vaisakh’s case his release point and arm path were different from his earlier action. I made slight adjustments to his loading and recoil and things fell into place,” Biju.explained.
Vaisakh struck a fine rhythm during Kerala’s practice matches against Jammu and Kashmir and against Hyderabad, picking up wickets which brought him back into contention for Ranji Trophy. He out-bowled his senior partners Jalaj Saxena and Aditya Sarvate on a flat track in Jamshedpur to take a five-wicket haul. Against Odisha too, Vaisakh was the highest wicket-taker in the first innings.
“Coach (Swapnil) Asnodkar sir asked me to bowl a little slower through the air, and I followed it. Now I am able to extract more from the surface, and by mixing the pace I can confuse the batters. Bowling in tandem with Jalaj and Sarvate has been incredibly helpful for learning about field settings and the type of deliveries to bowl to specific batters. They are always there to help me. And sometimes we plot the dismissal of a batter together, “ he said.

The order was issued by the Local Self Government Department a day before the Blasters are scheduled to host Mumbai City FC in their first home match of the season. The stadium is owned by the Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA).
The government has also fixed a security deposit of Rs 25 lakh for the use of the stadium.
In its order, the government said it had considered the club's request and recognised Kerala Blasters' role in the growth of football in the state and in encouraging youngsters to take an interest in sports.
It also noted the contribution of the club and the ISL to the development of sports infrastructure in the state. Supporting Kerala Blasters, one of the state's prominent football clubs, was in the public interest, the order said.
The Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium has been Kerala Blasters' home ground since the ISL began in 2014.
The Blasters will host Mumbai City FC on Sunday as they look to bounce back from a 4-1 defeat to NorthEast United FC. 
Mumbai City, meanwhile, will be chasing their first win of the season after collecting just one point from their opening two matches.
Kerala head coach Ashley Westwood acknowledged the defensive mistakes that contributed to the defeat but said the team was still settling into the season. With limited time together during pre-season, the Blasters are working on building combinations and settling on a consistent starting eleven.
Westwood, however, said his side would continue to play an attacking game.
"We try and play intense, aggressive football. We try and get numbers forward. We try and win every game," he said.
